evidence: Opened the landing page and read it top to bottom: hero, six feature boxes, quote, video block, footer
Opened the pricing page, read the plan table and the small print under it, expanded the four FAQ questions by reading their text
Looked at the pricing page rendered at laptop width and at phone width (390 px)
Opened the sign-up page and read every field, the step line and the sentence above the button
Tried the Starter 'Start free' button and the 14-day trial buttons: all go to the same sign-up form with card fields
Opened the privacy page and read all five points
Read the page styling for text colours and the red/green tag colours, and for what happens to the table below 760 px
Did not type anything into the form and stopped at the card number field
name: Harald Nygaard
background: Self-employed electrician, lives alone, cooks properly and wastes little. Arrived by mistake from a search for a pantry shelving unit.
history: Has been sold subscriptions for things a notebook does, and resents it.
first_10s: Hylle. Jeg lette etter en hylle til spiskammerset, ikke en app. 'Know what's in the fridge before you shop.' Jeg vet hva som er i kjoleskapet mitt, jeg apner det. Phone picture with 'Dijon mustard x3 stop!' Ha. Fine, that one is a bit true. But 'shared with Sam, Priya and Jo' - I live alone. This is not for me. Button says free trial, and a trial usually means a card. Let me see the price before I leave.
journey: Landed on the front page expecting shelves, found a pantry list app. Almost left at once.
Read the feature boxes. Scan, nudges, shared list, shopping list: all things a notebook and a magnet on the fridge do. 'Partner offers based on your pantry' made me stop for a second.
Clicked Pricing. Headline says $3.99 per month. Small grey print under the table says billed annually, $47.88 a year. So the big number is not what I would pay per month.
Opened the FAQ. Monthly is $5.99, not $3.99. Asked 'why do you need my card' and the answer does not answer it.

Pressed Start free on the Starter plan, the one that says $0. It went to the same sign-up as the trial: email, a password of twelve characters, and card number, expiry, CVC. So the free plan is not free to start.
Read the line above the button: no charge today, then Household at $47.88 a year starts after the trial. I never chose Household, it was chosen for me.
Read the privacy page. Anonymised and aggregated shopping insights go to retail and brand partners, and the sign-up says agreeing to the terms includes partner offers. Closed it.

At phone width the plan table is wider than the screen: only Starter shows, and the Household and Family+ columns with the trial button are cut off to the right. A person on a phone sees the free plan and a sliver of the next one.
Stopped at the card number field. Did not type anything.

blockers: Every route to the product, including the $0 Starter plan, ends at a form that asks for card number, expiry and CVC. I could not find a way to try it without a card, so I stopped.
The front page says the web app works today but there is no link to it anywhere. 'Get the app' goes to the sign-up form, not to an app or a store.
The product tour video is a dark box saying coming soon, so there is no way to see what it does without paying details.
friction: $3.99 per month is the big number, but you are billed $47.88 for a year. Monthly is $5.99, and that is only found in the FAQ. Three different prices for the same plan.
Sign-up silently picks the Household plan. There is no plan choice on the form, and Starter and the trial go to the same page.
Step line says '3. Invite your household'. Nothing says what happens if you are one person.
The FAQ answer to 'why do you need my card' is 'it keeps the trial smooth', which is not a reason.

Small grey text on a light background is hard to read: the line under the headline, the small print about annual billing and auto-conversion, the note under the hero buttons. The 'trial converts to a paid annual plan' warning is in the faintest text on the page.
Expiry tags in the phone mock-up are red against green. I cannot tell 'warn' from 'plenty' by colour, only by the word, and some tags have no word that helps.
At phone width the plan table scrolls sideways and hides the paid plans and their buttons.

works: The headline is plain and I understood the idea in one read.
The price table is simple to read on a laptop: three columns, what you get, one button each.
The privacy page is short and in ordinary words. It tells me everybody in the household sees everything, and that receipts are kept 30 days.
The sign-up says 'you won't be charged today' near the top, and the pricing page says trial converts unless cancelled before day 14. At least it is written down.
The sign-up form is short and the labels are large enough to read.
fails: A free plan that wants a card is not a free plan. A $0 button leads to a card form.
The price is shown as per month but billed per year, with the truth in grey small print.
The data sharing is bundled into the sign-up agreement: 'including partner offers'. I am asked to agree to my pantry being turned into marketing data before I have seen the product.
Nothing on the site shows the product working: a drawn phone, a quote from an unnamed 'beta household of four', and a video that does not exist.
Footer says it is a fictional product for demonstrations. If so, who am I paying?
missing: A real way to use it with no card, for one person, and see the list.
An export, so my list is not locked in. A plain note on what I keep if I stop paying.
A clear statement that one person can use it alone and what the 50-item limit means in a real kitchen.
Where to cancel, and how, before I give the card.
A link to the web app that is said to work today.
A price in kroner, or at least a clear statement of tax for Norway.
said: Jeg lette etter en hylle, ikke et abonnement pa spiskammerset mitt.
A notebook on the door costs nothing and never asks for my card.
It says free for 14 days, then it wants a card number. That is not free, that is a trap with a calendar.
$3.99 a month, until you read the grey text and it is $47.88 a year up front. And $5.99 if you want to pay monthly. Pick one number and say it.
I pressed the button for the free plan and got asked for my credit card. Seriously.
'We will email you three days before your trial ends.' Fine. Then I have to remember to cancel. That is their whole business.
Partner offers based on what is in my pantry. No thanks. What I eat is none of a supermarket's business.
Do I really need an app to know I have three jars of mustard? Open the cupboard.
unsaid: The mustard joke landed. I have more than one jar of something and it irritated me that it was right. I would not tell anyone.
I live alone and the whole page is about sharing with Sam, Priya and Jo. It made my kitchen feel like the wrong kind of kitchen, a bit empty. I closed the tab rather than read more.

I could not tell the red tags from the green ones in the picture. I stopped trying to read the picture and just decided it was not for me. I would never say that I could not read it, I would just say it looked like nothing.

I read the grey print on the pricing page twice and had to lean in. A company that puts the thing I need to know in the lightest text on the page has decided I should not read it. That decided it for me more than the price did.

Hovered over the $0 button hoping it would be honest. When it went to a card form I felt a bit stupid for expecting otherwise, and that anger is why I would warn my friends off rather than just shrug.
I would not put my card in even if I wanted the product. I have been burned by trials I forgot to cancel and I do not trust myself on day 13.
The tab with the pantry shelf search is still open. This one is gone. I never did find a shelf.

verdict.why: I am not the target customer, and the site gave me no reason to become one. The only way in is a card form, even for the $0 plan. The price is quoted per month but charged per year. The data-sharing is tied into the sign-up. Everything it does, a pencil and a paper list does, for free.
verdict.what_would_flip: A real, working free version for one person with no card, a single honest price shown with the yearly figure first, and partner data sharing off by default and switched on only if I choose it. Even then I would probably keep the notebook.
